info.title: PhotoMem API
info.description: PhotoMem is a self-improving memory layer for LLM applications, enabling personalized AI experiences that save costs and delight users.

post.description: Create a new memory entry for a specific user. This endpoint stores conversational context, user preferences, or any relevant information that should be remembered for future interactions. Memories are automatically deduplicated by content hash and user ID combination.

value.content: Prefers dark mode and concise responses. Works in software engineering.
Discussed project timeline for Q1 2024. Prefers weekly updates on Fridays.

memory.content: Prefers dark mode and concise responses. Works in software engineering.

x-code-samples.source:
# Install the PhotoMem SDK:
# pip install photomem

from photomem import PhotoMemClient

client = PhotoMemClient(api_key="pm_your_api_key")

# Create a memory
memory = client.memories.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    user_name="John Doe",
    content="Prefers dark mode and concise responses. Works in software engineering.",
    tags=["preference", "settings"]
)

print(f"Memory created: {memory.id}")

curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/v1/memories \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer pm_your_api_key' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "userId": "user_123",
    "userName": "John Doe",
    "content": "Prefers dark mode and concise responses. Works in software engineering.",
    "tags": ["preference", "settings"]
  }'

get.description: Retrieve a paginated list of all memories for your project. Results are ordered by creation date (newest first). Use pagination parameters to navigate through large memory sets.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of memories to return per page. Maximum value is 100.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of memories to skip. Use for pagination (e.g., offset=20 to get the second page when limit=20).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Filter memories by specific user ID.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Filter memories by tags (comma-separated).

memories.content: Prefers dark mode and concise responses.

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

client = PhotoMemClient(api_key="pm_your_api_key")

# List all memories with pagination
memories = client.memories.list(
    limit=20,
    offset=0
)

print(f"Total memories: {memories.pagination['total']}")
for memory in memories.memories:
    print(f"- {memory.id}: {memory.content[:50]}...")

curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://api.photomem.ai/api/v1/memories?limit=20&offset=0' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer pm_your_api_key'

get.description: Retrieve a specific memory by its unique identifier. This endpoint returns the complete memory object including all metadata, tags, and timestamps.

parameters.name: memory_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the memory to retrieve. Memory IDs start with 'mem_' prefix.

memory.content: Prefers dark mode and concise responses. Works in software engineering.

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

client = PhotoMemClient(api_key="pm_your_api_key")

# Get a specific memory by ID
memory = client.memories.get("mem_a1b2c3d4e5f6")

print(f"Memory: {memory.content}")
print(f"User: {memory.userName}")
print(f"Tags: {', '.join(memory.tags)}")

curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/v1/memories/mem_a1b2c3d4e5f6 \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer pm_your_api_key'

patch.description: Update an existing memory's content and/or tags. You can update either field independently or both at once. The userId and userName fields cannot be modified. The updatedAt timestamp will be automatically refreshed.

parameters.name: memory_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the memory to update.

value.content: Prefers dark mode, concise responses, and async communication. Works in software engineering at a startup.
Updated memory content with more details.

memory.content: Prefers dark mode, concise responses, and async communication. Works in software engineering at a startup.

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

client = PhotoMemClient(api_key="pm_your_api_key")

# Update memory content and tags

  }'

delete.description: Permanently delete a specific memory by ID. This operation performs a soft delete, marking the memory as deleted rather than removing it from the database. The memory will no longer appear in queries or searches. This action cannot be undone.

parameters.name: memory_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the memory to delete.

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

client = PhotoMemClient(api_key="pm_your_api_key")

# Delete a memory
result = client.memories.delete("mem_a1b2c3d4e5f6")

print(f"Memory deleted: {result.message}")
print(f"Deleted at: {result.deletedAt}")

curl --request DELETE \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/v1/memories/mem_a1b2c3d4e5f6 \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer pm_your_api_key'

post.description: Perform semantic search across memories using natural language queries. This endpoint uses advanced embedding models to find memories that are contextually similar to your search query, even if they don't contain exact keyword matches. Perfect for retrieving relevant user context in conversational AI applications.

value.query: What are the user's preferences for UI design?

memory.content: Prefers dark mode and concise responses. Works in software engineering.
Likes minimalist UI with high contrast colors.

value.query: What are the user's preferences for UI design?

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

client = PhotoMemClient(api_key="pm_your_api_key")

# Search memories semantically
results = client.memories.search(
    query="What are the user's preferences for UI design?",
    limit=10,
    min_relevance=0.7
)

print(f"Found {results.totalResults} relevant memories:")
for result in results.results:
    print(f"- [{result.relevanceScore:.2f}] {result.memory.content}")

curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/v1/memories/search \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer pm_your_api_key' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "query": "What are the user'\''s preferences for UI design?",
    "limit": 10,
    "minRelevance": 0.7
  }'

get.description: Retrieve a list of all API keys for a specific project within an organization. This endpoint returns key metadata including name, prefix, status, permissions, and usage information. The full API key value is never returned for security reasons.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization. Organization IDs start with 'org_' prefix.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project. Project IDs start with 'proj_' prefix.

message.example: You don't have access to this organization

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# List all API keys for a project
api_keys = client.api_keys.list(
    org_id="org_abc123def456",
    project_id="proj_xyz789ghi012"
)

print(f"Found {len(api_keys.apiKeys)} API keys:")
for key in api_keys.apiKeys:
    print(f"- {key.name} ({key.keyPrefix}...) - Status: {key.status}")

curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456/projects/proj_xyz789ghi012/api-keys \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token'

post.description: Generate a new API key for authenticating requests to the PhotoMem API. The full API key is only displayed once upon creation - store it securely! You must be an admin or owner of the organization to create API keys. Keys can be scoped with specific permissions and optional expiration dates.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project.

production_key.summary: Production API key with read/write permissions

value.warning: This is the only time the full API key will be displayed. Store it securely.

message.example: You must be an admin to create API keys

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# Create a new API key
result = client.api_keys.create(
    org_id="org_abc123def456",
    project_id="proj_xyz789ghi012",
    name="Production API Key",
    permissions=["read", "write"]
)

print(f"API Key created: {result.apiKey.name}")
print(f"Full key (save this!): {result.apiKey.key}")
print(f"Warning: {result.warning}")

curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456/projects/proj_xyz789ghi012/api-keys \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "name": "Production API Key",
    "permissions": ["read", "write"],
    "expiresAt": null
  }'

delete.description: Permanently revoke an API key, immediately invalidating it for all future requests. This action cannot be undone. Any requests made with this key after revocation will return a 401 Unauthorized error. You must be an admin or owner of the organization to revoke API keys.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project.

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the API key to revoke.

message.example: You must be an admin to revoke API keys

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# Revoke an API key
result = client.api_keys.revoke(
    org_id="org_abc123def456",
    project_id="proj_xyz789ghi012",
    key_id="key_a1b2c3d4e5f6"
)

print(f"API key revoked: {result.message}")
print(f"Revoked at: {result.revokedAt}")

curl --request DELETE \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456/projects/proj_xyz789ghi012/api-keys/key_a1b2c3d4e5f6 \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token'

post.description: Generate a new API key to replace an existing one, with an optional grace period where both keys remain valid. This is useful for zero-downtime key rotation in production environments. You can specify a grace period (0-30 days) during which the old key continues to work, allowing you to update all services before the old key expires.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the project.

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the API key to rotate.

value.warning: The old API key will remain valid until 2024-01-26T11:00:00Z. Update your services before this date.

message.example: You must be an admin to rotate API keys

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# Rotate API key with 7-day grace period
result = client.api_keys.rotate(
    org_id="org_abc123def456",
    project_id="proj_xyz789ghi012",
    key_id="key_a1b2c3d4e5f6",
    grace_period_days=7
)

print(f"New API key: {result.newApiKey.key}")
print(f"Old key expires at: {result.oldApiKey.expiresAt}")
print(f"Warning: {result.warning}")

curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456/projects/proj_xyz789ghi012/api-keys/key_a1b2c3d4e5f6/rotate \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "gracePeriodDays": 7
  }'

get.description: Retrieve a list of all organizations that the authenticated user belongs to. Each organization includes details such as name, slug, plan information, member count, and the user's role within the organization. In the current version, users can only belong to one organization, but this endpoint is designed to support multiple organizations per user in the future.

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# List all organizations
result = client.organizations.list()

for org in result.organizations:
    print(f"{org.name} ({org.plan}) - Your role: {org.yourRole}")
    print(f"  Members: {org.memberCount}")

curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token'

post.description: Create a new organization. The authenticated user will automatically become the owner of the newly created organization. Organization names must be unique across the platform, and slugs are automatically generated from the name (lowercase, hyphenated). You can also set initial organization settings during creation.

slug.description: Optional custom slug (auto-generated if not provided)

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# Create a new organization
org = client.organizations.create(
    name="My Startup",
    settings={
        "allowGuestAccess": False,
        "defaultMemoryRetention": 90
    }
)

print(f"Organization created: {org.id}")
print(f"Slug: {org.slug}")

get.description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific organization, including settings, plan details, usage limits, and member statistics. You must be a member of the organization to access its details.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# Get organization details
org = client.organizations.get("org_abc123def456")

print(f"{org.name} ({org.plan})")
print(f"Members: {org.memberCount}, Projects: {org.projectCount}")
print(f"Your role: {org.yourRole}")

curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456 \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token'

delete.description: Permanently delete an organization and all its associated data, including projects, API keys, memories, and webhooks. This is a destructive operation that cannot be undone. Only organization owners can delete organizations. All members will lose access immediately.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization to delete.

message.example: Only organization owners can delete organizations

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# Delete organization
result = client.organizations.delete("org_abc123def456")

print(f"Organization deleted: {result.message}")
print(f"Deleted at: {result.deletedAt}")

curl --request DELETE \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456 \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token'

get.description: Retrieve a list of all members in an organization, including their roles, email addresses, status, and join dates. This endpoint is useful for displaying team rosters, managing access control, and auditing membership. You must be a member of the organization to view its member list.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

403.description: Forbidden - not a member of this organization

message.example: You don't have access to this organization

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# List organization members
result = client.organizations.get_members("org_abc123def456")

print(f"Total members: {result.totalMembers}")
for member in result.members:
    print(f"- {member.fullName} ({member.email}) - Role: {member.role}")

curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456/members \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token'

post.description: Invite a new member to join the organization by sending them an invitation email. You can specify their role (admin or member) at the time of invitation. Only organization admins and owners can invite new members. The invitee will receive an email with instructions to accept the invitation. Pending invitations expire after 7 days.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

email.description: Email address of the person to invite

role.description: Role to assign to the new member

message.description: Optional personal message to include in the invitation email
message.example: Welcome to the team! Looking forward to working with you.

value.message: We'd love to have you as an admin!

400.description: Bad request - validation error or user already exists

message.example: User is already a member of this organization
Only admins can invite new members

x-code-samples.source:
from photomem import PhotoMemClient

# Initialize with user authentication token
client = PhotoMemClient(auth_token="your_clerk_token")

# Invite a new member
invitation = client.organizations.invite_member(
    org_id="org_abc123def456",
    email="newmember@example.com",
    role="member",
    message="Welcome to the team!"
)

print(f"Invitation sent: {invitation.invitationId}")
print(f"Expires at: {invitation.expiresAt}")

curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.photomem.ai/api/organizations/org_abc123def456/members \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_clerk_token' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "email": "newmember@example.com",
    "role": "member",
    "message": "Welcome to the team!"
  }'
